findings.description: Section: Testing Strategy > CI; Task 9; Acceptance Criteria 'go test ./... запускается в CI и блокирует деплой при падении'. The stated mechanism does not exist in GitHub Actions. The spec says test.yml 'становится needs: для job деплоя в .github/workflows/deploy.yml'. `needs:` is a dependency between jobs inside one workflow file; a job in deploy.yml cannot declare `needs:` a job that lives in test.yml. Verified against the real file: .github/workflows/deploy.yml has exactly one job, `build-and-deploy` (line 13), triggered by `on: push: tags: - "*"` (lines 3-6). A workflow triggered by a tag push and a workflow triggered by branch push/PR are separate runs with no ordering relationship. Consequence: Task 9 will hit an impossible instruction and improvise — the likely improvisation is 'add test.yml, leave deploy.yml alone', which yields a green tests badge and a deploy path that still ships whatever is at the tag, tested or not. Tags are commonly pushed at commits that never went through a PR, so the deploy commit may have never run the suite at all. The acceptance criterion is then unverifiable as written, and the criterion above it ('Все существующие тесты проходят; регрессий в costing_test.go нет') keeps the exact non-enforcement the previous round flagged.
findings.recommendation: Replace the mechanism with the one GitHub actually provides: make test.yml a reusable workflow (`on: {push:, pull_request:, workflow_call:}`), then in deploy.yml add `jobs.test: {uses: ./.github/workflows/test.yml}` and `jobs.build-and-deploy.needs: test`. That is the only construct that makes a red suite block a tag deploy. Write the concrete job into the spec so Task 9 cannot improvise: `runs-on: ubuntu-latest`, `actions/checkout@v4`, `actions/setup-go@v5` with `go-version: 1.25.5` (matches server/go.mod), `working-directory: ./server`, `run: go test -race ./...`. Add `-race` explicitly — it is required for the fire-and-forget notifier goroutine (see the goroutine finding). Add a verification step to Task 9 that proves the gate works rather than that the file exists: push a commit with a deliberately failing test on a branch, tag it, and confirm the deploy job is skipped, not merely that the test job went red.

findings.description: Section: Testing Strategy > CI + Integration tests; Tasks 3 and 4. The TEST_DB_DSN skip pattern will silently skip in CI, making the contract set theatre for every run after the implementing agent's session. Three converging facts: (1) the CI subsection plans only `setup-go` + `go test ./...` with no `services:` block, and states outright 'Все тесты, кроме помеченных TEST_DB_DSN, герметичны и в CI не требуют БД' — i.e. the plan of record is that CI runs with no database; (2) `t.Skip` makes the package report `ok`, so a CI run where the entire PostgresRepository contract set and all of auth/store_test.go never executed is byte-identical in output to one where they passed; (3) the only place they actually run is Task 3's and Task 4's Verify-smoke, executed once, by hand, by the implementing agent. So the production storage layer — the layer RequireAdmin reads its authorization decision from — and the session-identity round trip get one manual execution during construction and zero regression protection forever after. That is exactly the state the previous round called critical; the restructure into a factory made the tests runnable against MariaDB but nothing in the plan makes them run. Task 3's own smoke command makes it worse: `TEST_DB_DSN=... go test ./internal/repository/...` has no `-v`, so a skipped run and a passing run print the same `ok` line, and the Verify-smoke expectation 'контрактный набор проходит против MariaDB, а не только пропускается' cannot be judged from that command's output. Note also that the handler tests substitute a stubbed session resolver, so with store_test.go skipped, the chain cookie → real auth.Store lookup → identity in context has no automated coverage in CI at any level.
findings.recommendation: Make the DB-backed set run in CI and make skipping loud. (1) In test.yml add a service container: `services: {mariadb: {image: mariadb:11.4, env: {MARIADB_ROOT_PASSWORD: root, MARIADB_DATABASE: poshivon}, ports: ['3306:3306'], options: --health-cmd="healthcheck.sh --connect" --health-interval=5s --health-retries=10}}` and set `env: TEST_DB_DSN: root:root@tcp(127.0.0.1:3306)/poshivon?multiStatements=true&parseTime=true` on the test step. GitHub-hosted ubuntu-latest supports service containers natively — no self-hosted runner, no secrets. (2) Make the skip fail-loud where a DB is expected: in the helper that reads the DSN, `if dsn == "" { if os.Getenv("CI") != "" { t.Fatal("TEST_DB_DSN must be set in CI") }; t.Skip(...) }`. Without this guard a later edit to the workflow silently reverts the whole tier. (3) Fix both Verify-smoke commands to be judgeable: `go test -v -run 'TestUserRepositoryContract|TestAccessRequestRepositoryContract' ./internal/repository/... | tee /tmp/out; grep -c -- '--- SKIP' /tmp/out` → expect 0 SKIP lines and the Postgres sub-run present by name. Same for `./internal/auth/...`. (4) Amend the CI subsection's claim: it currently asserts hermeticity as a reason not to provision a DB; state instead that the DSN-gated tier is the only coverage of production storage and therefore must be provisioned.

findings.description: Decision 8 / Task 4 / Task 5; Testing Strategy > Integration tests, single bullet 'Изменяющий запрос с посторонним Origin → 403 и флаг не изменился'. RequireSameOrigin has four branches and exactly one is tested — and it is the branch whose failure is harmless. Decision 8 specifies: mutating method + foreign Origin → 403; mutating method + **absent** Origin → 403; GET/HEAD → exempt; empty CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS → check skipped entirely. Untested: the absent-Origin branch (explicitly called out in Decision 8 and the branch most likely to be coded wrong); the GET/HEAD exemption; the empty-list dev bypass; and most importantly the **positive** branch — an allowed Origin on a mutating request must pass through. That positive branch now guards every write in the product, because Decision 6 puts RequireSameOrigin in front of /api/v1/users/ too: POST settings, POST chats, DELETE chats/{id}, POST calculate, POST market-feedback. A RequireSameOrigin that rejects the legitimate production origin takes the entire application down for writes, and nothing in the test list fails. There is a second, concrete inconsistency: AVP item 2 drives the whole scenario with curl, and curl sends no Origin header. Under the spec's own rule, every POST in that scenario is a 403 unless CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS happens to be empty in the dev environment — but if it is empty the check is skipped, so the AVP's 'изменяющий запрос с посторонним Origin отклонён' step returns 2xx and fails. The AVP as written cannot pass in either configuration.
findings.recommendation: Replace the single bullet with a table-driven middleware test over (method, Origin header, configured allowlist), run through the same route-building function as main.go, asserting both status and storage state: (a) allowlist=['https://app.example'], POST with Origin: https://app.example → not 403, and the write took effect (repo state changed); (b) same allowlist, POST with Origin: https://evil.example → 403 AND repo state unchanged; (c) same allowlist, POST with **no** Origin header → 403 AND repo state unchanged; (d) same allowlist, GET with Origin: https://evil.example → 200 (exemption holds); (e) allowlist=[] , POST with Origin: https://evil.example → not 403 (dev bypass, and pin it so nobody 'hardens' it into a prod-breaking default by accident). Run (a)-(c) against at least one existing product route (POST /api/v1/users/settings) as well as the admin grant route, since Decision 6 newly subjects product writes to this check. Fix the AVP: state that the curl scenario runs with CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS set to the dev origin and that every mutating curl passes `-H 'Origin: http://localhost:5173'`, with two explicit negatives — one curl omitting the header and one with a foreign value — each followed by a DB read-back proving no state change.

findings.description: Section: Testing Strategy > Unit tests > notifier_test.go (now marked Phase 2). This finding is not closed — the bullets are unchanged word for word from the version I reviewed in round 1; the only edit is a '(Phase 2)' tag. Deferring a defective test plan to a later phase does not fix it, and Phase 2's Task 16 still lists test-reviewer as a reviewer of these same bullets. 'Тело письма содержит логин и email заявителя' remains a substring-presence assertion: it passes on a byte string that is nothing but the login and email concatenated, with no headers, no CRLF separator between headers and body, and no valid RFC 5322 structure. The failure modes that actually occur when hand-rolling net/smtp messages — missing blank line between headers and body, un-encoded 8-bit Subject, malformed To list — all survive it. 'Тема письма с кириллицей кодируется в RFC 2047 encoded-word' is likewise almost certainly written as a prefix/substring check for '=?UTF-8?' rather than a decode. And there is still no header-injection test: the message is built from a Yandex-supplied login and email, net/smtp performs no sanitization, and a CRLF in either field injects arbitrary headers (Bcc, forged From) into mail sent to both administrators. security-auditor is a listed reviewer on Task 16 and the test plan hands it nothing to verify.
findings.recommendation: Replace substring checks with a round-trip parse — net/mail is already declared in Dependencies. Build the message, `msg, err := mail.ReadMessage(bytes.NewReader(raw))` (an unparseable message fails here instead of silently passing a Contains check), then assert: `(&mime.WordDecoder{}).DecodeHeader(msg.Header.Get("Subject"))` equals the exact expected Russian subject string; `msg.Header.Get("To")` equals the configured admin list verbatim; the body read from msg.Body equals the exact expected rendered text for a fixed login/email pair. Add the injection case as a required bullet: build a message for login "ivan\r\nBcc: attacker@evil.com" and assert either that construction returns an error, or that the parsed message has no Bcc header and the login appears only in the body with control characters stripped. For the no-email case assert the parsed body's exact content, not the absence of a substring.

findings.description: Task 6; Testing Strategy > server/internal/handler/http_test.go. Task 6 rewrites the path parsing of nine distinct route/method branches, and the test list names exactly one of them. Read server/internal/handler/http.go:26-70: handleUsers derives `userID := parts[0]` and `resource := parts[1]`, and the nine branches then key off `len(parts) == 2/3/4` and `parts[2]`/`parts[3]`. Removing the userID segment shifts every index by one and changes every length comparison in all nine cases: POST/GET settings, POST/GET chats, DELETE chats/{id}, POST chats/{id}/restore, POST chats/{id}/calculate, GET chats/{id}/calculations, POST market-feedback. The test list covers `GET /api/v1/users/chats`. An off-by-one that lands, say, restore or calculations in the `default:` 404 branch, or a branch left reading the owner from the address, ships green. This is the highest-density mechanical-error surface in Phase 1 and it has one test.
findings.recommendation: Make http_test.go table-driven over the complete route table rather than one representative. One table of {method, path, body} covering all nine branches, each row run three times: (1) no cookies → 401 for every row; (2) session for a user with has_access=false → 403 for every row; (3) session for a user with access → not 404 and not 401/403, i.e. the route still resolves after reindexing (assert the specific success code each branch returns: 200 for the GETs, 201/200 for chat creation, 204 for settings and delete). Add the write-side ownership assertion the current list omits — it asserts only that reads return the caller's data: as user 'ivan', POST a chat, then as user 'petr' assert GET chats does not contain it and DELETE of ivan's chat id returns 404/403 and leaves the chat present in the repository. Ownership on the write paths is the half of Decision 6 that currently has no test at all.

findings.description: Decision 9 (OAuth state); Task 7; Acceptance Criteria. The `state` parameter is a security control added by this feature and it is verified by nothing, anywhere. There is no unit test (client tests are None by decision), no handler test (it is entirely client-side), no acceptance criterion — the AC list's only US-17 item is 'POST /auth/yandex возвращает 404' — and no AVP step. AVP item 3 exercises panel rendering only; Task 7's Verify-user says 'выйти и войти заново → вход проходит успешно', which walks the happy path where state matches, i.e. the one path that would also succeed if AuthCallback ignored state entirely or compared it to itself. The branch that is the entire point of the parameter — state absent from sessionStorage, or present and different from the one returned in the callback URL, must abort the exchange before the code is sent — is confirmed by no one. A no-op comparison (a common bug: reading the stored key after having already cleared it, so both sides are empty strings and compare equal) is indistinguishable from a correct implementation under every check in this spec.
findings.recommendation: Add an acceptance criterion and a manual verification step, since the client tier has no test runner by decision. AC: 'Возврат из OAuth со значением `state`, не совпадающим с сохранённым, прерывает вход: обмена кода на токен не происходит, сессия не создаётся'. Verify-user on Task 7, which is cheap and does not need a test runner: start login normally, and on the callback URL edit the `state` query parameter in the address bar before it is processed (or overwrite the sessionStorage key via devtools), reload, and assert the panel does not log in AND the Network tab shows no request to /auth/yandex/code. Add the empty-stored-state case explicitly: clear the sessionStorage key, then load a callback URL carrying a state value → login must be refused, not accepted. Add the negative to Task 15's post-deploy list as a curl-level or Playwright-level check so the control is confirmed at least once on the live environment.

findings.description: Decision 10; Task 4 (middleware); Acceptance Criteria 'Пользователь с role=admin и has_access=false проходит проверку доступа'. The rule `has_access || role == 'admin'` is implemented in two places — the service (AccessState for GET /access/me) and RequireAccess in middleware.go, per the Architecture section 'RequireAccess ... пропускает дальше только при has_access || role == \'admin\'' — and it is tested in only one. The Unit tests list has 'Пользователь с ролью admin и has_access=false считается имеющим доступ (US-14)', which exercises the service copy on stubs. No handler or middleware test puts an admin with has_access=false through a route guarded by RequireAccess. That is the copy that matters: if RequireAccess is written as a plain `if !user.HasAccess { 403 }`, an administrator whose flag was never set — which is every administrator created by the migration's INSERT if the has_access column is ever changed, and any admin promoted later — is locked out of all product data while GET /access/me cheerfully reports role=admin. The acceptance criterion is written in the middleware's language ('проходит проверку доступа') and is claimed by a test of a different component.
findings.recommendation: Add to middleware_test.go / access_test.go, built through the same route-assembly function as main.go: seed the repository with a user {role: 'admin', has_access: false}, then with that session (a) GET /api/v1/users/chats → 200, not 403 — this is the acceptance criterion at the layer that enforces it; (b) GET /api/v1/admin/users → 200; (c) GET /api/v1/access/me → 200 with has_access:false in the body but the client-side gate satisfied by role, pinning that the two copies of the rule agree on the same fixture. Add the mirror case so the rule cannot be satisfied by a middleware that just always passes: {role:'user', has_access:false} → GET /api/v1/users/chats → 403.

findings.description: Acceptance Criteria 'Строка users появляется после входа, до каких-либо действий в панели'; Decision 11; Task 4. Still unowned after the rewrite — no test, no AVP step, no post-deploy item. The whole of Decision 11 exists because without it the admin list is empty for exactly the users the feature serves and the access_requests foreign key has nothing to point at, and the login path that calls AccessService.EnsureUser (HandleYandexCode in server/internal/handler/auth.go, modified by Task 4) is not exercised by any test in the plan. The handler test list covers /access/*, /admin/* and /api/v1/users/* but never the login handler. The contract set covers EnsureUser at the repository level, which proves the repository behaves — not that the login handler ever calls it, and 'the call was forgotten' is precisely the failure this criterion guards. AVP item 2's curl scenario starts from an already-established session, so it cannot observe row creation at login either.
findings.recommendation: Two places, both cheap. (1) A handler test for the login path with the Yandex profile fetch stubbed: drive HandleYandexCode to success, then assert `repo.ListUsers()` contains the new login with role=='user' and has_access==false, AND that no settings/chats/calculations rows exist for it — the criterion's 'до каких-либо действий в панели' clause. If the Yandex HTTP call cannot be stubbed cleanly, at minimum test the extracted function that Task 4 already creates ('вынос проверки сессии в переиспользуемый вид') and assert the same repository state. (2) Add to Task 15 (post-deploy) as a user-verified item: after the first real admin login, `docker exec poshivon_db mariadb ... -e "SELECT id, role, has_access FROM users WHERE id='RoGogDBD'"` returns the row with role='admin' — this simultaneously confirms row creation at login and that EnsureUser did not demote the migration-seeded admin on a real database, which is the one place that invariant meets production data.

findings.description: Section: Testing Strategy > Integration tests > access_repo_test.go; Unit tests bullet 'SetAccess для несуществующего логина: ErrNotFound'. The contract set gained the admin-demotion regression (good, that was the round-1 critical) but three invariants from the round-1 recommendation did not make it in, and two of them leave live litmus failures. (a) `GetUser` on an absent login is not in the contract list at all. The service unit tests can only assert what their stub returns, so nothing pins whether the real repositories return ErrNotFound or a zero-value UserRecord. A zero-value return turns 'user does not exist' into 'user with empty role and has_access=false' — silently a non-admin instead of an error — and it is the read RequireAccess and RequireAdmin both perform on every request. (b) `SetAccess` on an unknown login: 'ErrNotFound' appears only as a service unit test on a stub. If AccessService.SetAccess forwards to the repository (and there is no described service logic that would not), the stub returns ErrNotFound and the test asserts ErrNotFound — remove the service body and the test still passes. The behaviour lives in the repository and the repository contract set does not cover it, so the 404 branch of POST /admin/users/{unknown}/access rests on a tautology plus one handler test against MemoryRepository. (c) The granted=false direction is folded into one ambiguous bullet, 'SetAccess меняет флаг и виден последующему GetUser'. Round 1 asked for it explicitly because GORM `Updates` with a struct skips zero values, so `SetAccess(login, false)` silently no-ops on MariaDB while working perfectly in MemoryRepository — a bug class the memory implementation structurally cannot reproduce, and the exact mechanism by which US-10 (revocation) fails in production only.
findings.recommendation: Add three explicit bullets to the contract set, all running against both factories: (1) `GetUser` для несуществующего логина возвращает ErrNotFound, а не нулевой UserRecord — assert `errors.Is(err, service.ErrNotFound)` and that the returned record is not silently usable; (2) `SetAccess` для несуществующего логина возвращает ErrNotFound и не создаёт строку — assert the error AND that `len(ListUsers())` is unchanged; (3) split the flag bullet into a directional round-trip: EnsureUser → SetAccess(true) → GetUser().HasAccess == true → **SetAccess(false)** → GetUser().HasAccess == false, with a comment naming the GORM zero-value pitfall so nobody collapses it back into one assertion. Delete or repurpose the service-level 'SetAccess для несуществующего логина: ErrNotFound' bullet — keep a service test only if the service adds something the repository does not (e.g. that it does not call DecideRequest when the user is missing, read off the stub's recorded calls).

findings.description: Task 4 vs Task 5, Files to modify. Task 4 creates the entire authorization mechanism — RequireAuth, RequireAccess, RequireAdmin, RequireSameOrigin, identity in context — plus the 403/409 branches and the fixed-500 text in writeAPIDomainError, and its Files to modify list contains exactly one test file, `server/internal/auth/store_test.go`, which tests the session store and nothing else. `middleware_test.go` is created in Task 5 (a later wave) and `http_test.go` in Task 6 (later still). So every authorization rule in the feature ships from Task 4 with zero tests written in the session that wrote it, and Task 4's listed test-reviewer has only the store test to review. This violates the methodology's core rule that tests are written in the same session as the code, and it has a practical cost specific to the wave layout: a defect in RequireAccess or in the fixed-500 branch is discovered one to two waves later, when Task 5 or Task 6 writes the test — at which point the fix reopens a task that already passed review. It also means the 500-leak acceptance criterion, whose code is written in Task 4, has no owner until Task 5.
findings.recommendation: Move `server/internal/handler/middleware_test.go` into Task 4's Files to modify and state its scope there: the four middlewares exercised directly with httptest against a trivial terminal handler plus MemoryRepository and the stub session resolver — 401 no cookie, 401 session with empty yandex_login, 403 no access, 200 with access, 403 non-admin on an admin-gated handler, and the full RequireSameOrigin table from the Origin finding. Add the writeAPIDomainError branch tests to Task 4 as well (ErrForbidden→403, ErrConflict→409, unknown error→500 with the fixed body), since that function is edited there. Leave Task 5 owning access_test.go, which tests the assembled routes end to end — that split gives each task tests for the code it writes and keeps Task 5's route-assembly assertions meaningful rather than doubling as the first test of the middleware.

findings.description: Section: Testing Strategy > server/internal/auth/store_test.go; Decision 2. The new store test closes the rotation gap (good) but drops the sub-case the round-1 recommendation named as the one most likely to break: a session row created before the migration, with all three identity columns NULL, must round-trip out of FindByRefreshHash as a valid Session with an empty login and must not error on Scan. That is Decision 2's entire contract and it is where sql.NullString handling fails — scanning NULL into a plain string returns 'converting NULL to string is unsupported', which surfaces not as a clean 401 session_identity_missing but as a 500 on every request from every pre-existing session immediately after deploy. The handler-level bullet 'GET /api/v1/access/me с сессией без yandex_login → 401 session_identity_missing' does not cover this, because the handler tests use a stubbed session resolver — the stub returns a Go struct with an empty string and never touches a NULL column. Combined with store_test.go being TEST_DB_DSN-gated and (per the CI finding) never running in CI, the entire NULL path is verified by nobody at any point.
findings.recommendation: Add the bullet to store_test.go: insert a session row directly via raw SQL with yandex_login, yandex_email and yandex_display_name all NULL (simulating a pre-migration row), then FindByRefreshHash on its hash must return a Session with no error and YandexLogin == "" — assert `err == nil` explicitly, since the failure mode is an error and not a wrong value. Add the AVP step round 1 asked for and that is still missing from AVP item 2: after establishing a session, POST /auth/refresh to force a rotation, then GET /api/v1/access/me and assert it still returns the login rather than 401 session_identity_missing — this is the only place identity-survives-rotation is observed against a real database in the enabled configuration.

findings.description: Acceptance Criteria 'UpsertSettings, CreateChat и расчёт работают для нового пользователя после добавления колонок с CHECK-констрейнтом' vs the contract bullet 'Существующие пути записи не сломаны: UpsertSettings и CreateChat для нового пользователя проходят'. The criterion names three write paths and the test names two. The third, the calculation path, calls upsertUser at server/internal/repository/postgres.go:363 — the same call site as the other two and therefore subject to the same chk_users_role failure that Decision 13 documents as reproduced on live MariaDB (ERROR 4025). Dropping it from the test list is arbitrary; it is one more line in a suite that already has the fixtures set up.
findings.recommendation: Extend the bullet to all three call sites listed in Decision 13 (postgres.go:140, 233, 363): for a login that has never been seen, UpsertSettings, CreateChat and AppendCalculation each succeed, and afterwards GetUser on that login returns role=='user' (not empty), proving the row was created through the legacy userModel path without violating the CHECK and without leaving a role value the authorization read cannot interpret.

findings.description: Section: Testing Strategy > Integration tests, bullet 'Ошибка репозитория с SQL-текстом внутри → 500 без этого текста в теле' (Decision 17, AC 'Ответ 500 не содержит текста внутренней ошибки'). The assertion is absence-only. A handler that returns 500 with an empty body, or that panics into a 500 with no body, satisfies 'без этого текста' perfectly while breaking the client contract. Round 1 asked for the exact expected payload to be pinned as well, so the test doubles as the contract for the fixed text; that half was not adopted.
findings.recommendation: Assert both directions: the response body does NOT contain the injected secret-shaped fragments ('password', '3306', the raw error string) AND the body equals the exact fixed payload the contour returns, e.g. `{"error":"internal_error"}`, with Content-Type application/json. Use a repository stub returning `errors.New("dial tcp 10.0.0.5:3306: connection refused, user=poshivon password=poshivon")` so the negative assertion has something real to catch.

findings.description: Section: Testing Strategy > Integration tests, bullet 'POST /api/v1/admin/users/{unknown}/access администратором → 404 и ни один флаг не изменился'. The state assertion was added (good) but weakened from what was recommended: 'ни один флаг не изменился' checks the flags of rows that exist and says nothing about a row being created for the unknown login. A handler or repository that upserts the target before checking existence — the natural shape if SetAccess is implemented with GORM's Save or an ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE — creates a brand-new user row with has_access set and then returns 404, and this bullet passes. That is an admin-facing privilege-creation bug reachable by typing a login that does not exist.
findings.recommendation: Add the count assertion to the bullet: `len(ListUsers())` before the request equals `len(ListUsers())` after, and `GetUser(unknownLogin)` still returns ErrNotFound. Pair it with the repository-level bullet from the ErrNotFound finding so it is pinned at both layers.

findings.description: Decision 14; Phase 2 bullets 'ошибка нотификатора при создании заявки → ответ по-прежнему 201' and 'nil-нотификатор → ответ 201, отправки нет'. The tests were added — that closes the missing-coverage half of the round-1 finding — but the flakiness half is untouched: the notification is sent from a bare goroutine after the response is written, so both tests return while that goroutine is still running. 'отправки нет' in particular is a negative assertion on a racing goroutine, which is the definition of a nondeterministic test: it passes because the assertion runs before the send would have happened, not because no send occurs. There is still no synchronization seam in the design (no WaitGroup, no injectable done channel), and the CI plan does not run with -race, so the resulting failures will appear as unexplained intermittent CI reds attributed to 'flaky tests'. Two bullets also under-assert: 201 is checked but not that the request was durably created despite the notifier failure, which is the actual user-spec constraint.
findings.recommendation: Give the notifier an injectable interface at the handler boundary and use a stub that writes to a buffered channel on Send. Failure case: stub returns an error, assert 201 AND `repo.GetRequest(login).Status == "pending"` AND select on the channel with a 1s timeout to confirm Send was actually attempted with the requesting user's login and email (turning a fire-and-forget side effect into verified behaviour). Nil case: assert 201, the request exists, no panic, and — instead of racing — assert on a completion signal the handler exposes, or drop the 'отправки нет' claim, which cannot be asserted reliably against a goroutine. Add `-race` to the CI test command (see the CI finding) so this class surfaces as a real failure rather than intermittently.

findings.description: Section: Testing Strategy > Client tests. The 'None' declaration with justification is the route round 1 explicitly offered, and dropping test-reviewer from Tasks 7 and 8 is the honest follow-through — that part is closed. What is not honest is the cost claim: 'создание клиентской тестовой инфраструктуры кратно превышает объём фичи'. vitest + jsdom + @testing-library/react is one devDependency install, a four-line vite config `test` block, and one npm script — smaller than Task 9's scope, and requiring no CI job and no browser. Set against that: Tasks 7 and 8 are two of the fifteen Phase 1 tasks and implement the gate itself. The consequence the spec should state plainly is that the no-access branch of the Panel status machine, the effect guards preventing a gated user from fetching /settings, /chats and /calculations, the admin-only nav item (US-12), and the state check from Decision 9 all ship with zero regression protection and are confirmed once, by a human reading a Network tab, per deploy. The risks table itself flags those effect guards as fragile because they key on `profile` rather than `status` — a known-fragile guard with a once-per-deploy manual check is a thin control.
findings.recommendation: Keep the 'None' decision if the orchestrator accepts the cost, but correct the justification to state the real trade-off rather than an inflated setup cost: 'клиентская часть выкатывается без регрессионной защиты; все клиентские критерии проверяются вручную один раз за выкатку'. If any budget is available, the highest-value three tests remain the ones round 1 named — render Panel with a stubbed accessApi for {has_access:false, role:'user'} asserting the banner renders, the working interface does not, and the injected panelApi stub was never called with /settings or /chats; {has_access:false, role:'admin'} asserting the working interface and the Пользователи item both render (Decision 10 in the UI); {has_access:true, role:'user'} asserting the Пользователи item is absent (the only assertion of US-12 outside a manual step).

findings.description: Acceptance Criteria 'В выкаченной миграции нет плейсхолдера ADMIN_LOGIN_2; администраторов ровно два' and 'CONTACT_EMAIL доходит до контейнера и виден на плашке'. Both criteria are two-part and only the first part of each has a verification step. Task 9's Verify-smoke greps for the ADMIN_LOGIN_2 string, which proves the placeholder was replaced but says nothing about the resulting count — a typo in the substituted login, or a third admin left over from testing, produces a green grep and an admin roster that nobody counted. For CONTACT_EMAIL, `docker exec poshivon_app env | grep CONTACT_EMAIL` proves the variable reaches the container; nothing checks that the value reaches the banner, and AVP item 3 asserts only 'видна плашка' without reading its contents — which matters more than usual here, because the phase split makes that contact address the sole channel by which a user requests access until Phase 2 ships the notification email.
findings.recommendation: Add to Task 15 (post-deploy): `SELECT id FROM users WHERE role='admin'` returns exactly two rows and both are the intended logins — a count assertion, not a grep. Extend AVP item 3's no-access state to assert the banner displays the configured CONTACT_EMAIL value (Playwright text assertion against the same value passed to the container), so the criterion's second clause has an owner.

findings.description: Two reviewer-assignment inconsistencies left by the round-2 edits. (1) Task 1 (SQL migration) still lists test-reviewer among its reviewers while its Files to modify contains only 004_access_control.up.sql — there is no test artifact to review, which is precisely the reasoning used to drop test-reviewer from the client tasks; applied consistently it should be dropped here too (the migration's behaviour is covered by Task 3's contract set and the Verify-smoke idempotency run). (2) The inverse: Task 9 authors .github/workflows/test.yml — the file that determines whether any test in this feature ever runs again — and its reviewers are code-reviewer, security-auditor and deploy-reviewer, with no test-reviewer. Given that both critical findings in this review are about that file's contents, it is the one task where a test reviewer has the most to catch. Separately, the subsection heading 'Integration tests' still covers httptest + MemoryRepository + stubbed session resolver tests, which are wide unit tests; with the DSN-gated tier added the label is now merely imprecise rather than misleading, but it still lets a reader price the handler tier as DB-crossing coverage.
findings.recommendation: Drop test-reviewer from Task 1 and add it to Task 9 with an explicit brief: verify that the deploy job genuinely cannot run when tests fail, that TEST_DB_DSN is set in the workflow environment, and that no test in the suite is skipped in a CI run. Split the Testing Strategy subsection into 'Handler tests (httptest + in-memory)' and 'DB-backed contract tests (TEST_DB_DSN)' so the two tiers are priced separately.

findings.description: Agent Verification Plan item 2. The revoke step was added to the scenario chain ('отзыв доступа → тот же запрос данных отклонён (403)') — that closes the round-1 omission — but the database read-back that made the step worth adding was not. Asserting only that a later API call returns 403 confirms the middleware's view; it does not confirm the write landed. The specific bug it was meant to catch is a SetAccess implemented with GORM Updates over a struct, where granted=false is Go's zero value and is silently dropped: the flag stays 1 in the database while an in-process cache or the memory repository behaves correctly. Without a SELECT, the 403 could equally come from any other cause in the chain.
findings.recommendation: After the revoke POST in AVP item 2, add `docker exec poshivon_db mariadb -uposhivon -pposhivon poshivon -e "SELECT has_access FROM users WHERE id='<login>'"` expecting 0, and a GET /api/v1/access/me for that user expecting has_access:false in the body. Combine with the directional round-trip added to the repository contract set (see the ErrNotFound/granted=false finding) so the failure is caught by a test rather than only by this one-shot walkthrough.
